Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a reticulo-nodular pattern and nodular opacities predominantly in the upper and middle lung zones (perihilar and left mid/upper zones), which is the classic radiographic distribution for pulmonary sarcoidosis. Other options describe findings typical of different pathologies (e.g., cavitation suggests TB or fungal infection, consolidation suggests pneumonia) or are not visible on this film.
